findings.title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() breaks compilation
findings.body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only definition, added in `UsernamePasswordForm`, is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. There is no no-arg overload, so the `services` module will not compile. The call should pass `context.getUser()`.

findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, which disables passkeys on the initial login page
findings.body: The helper returns true only when `user != null`. `authenticate()` and `challenge(context, error, field)` use it to decide whether to call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm`. On a normal first login the user is null, so the conditional-UI/passkey attributes are no longer set. The old code did the opposite and set them when `context.getUser() == null`. This breaks passkey login for fresh logins, including the discoverable-key and external-key paths that the existing tests cover. Failed-login re-renders also lose the passkey data, because the user is usually cleared after a bad password. The intent is presumably to enable passkeys both for unidentified users and for re-authentication, so the `user != null` condition looks inverted or incomplete.

findings.title: Overriding method lacks @Override
findings.body: `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` overrides `WebAuthnAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` but has no `@Override` annotation. A future signature change in the parent would silently turn it into a non-override, and re-authentication would start showing the allowed-authenticator list again.

findings.title: Fragile try/catch(Exception) pattern for asserting element absence
findings.body: The test calls `findElement(...)` inside `try`, asserts `nullValue()`, then `fail(...)`, and catches `Exception`. The expected `NoSuchElementException` is swallowed. A `WebDriverException` from some other cause would also be swallowed, so the test can pass for the wrong reason. `fail` throws `AssertionError`, which is not an `Exception`, so it does propagate, but the check is still imprecise. Use `driver.findElements(...).isEmpty()` or `assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)`.
